ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High macro-level contrast; approximately 80% high-intensity white pixels on lateral lobes versus 20% low-intensity black pixels concentrated in the central peduncle-to-notch axis.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Central low-intensity black zone forms a wide 'Y' shape extending from the fluke base to the median notch. Lateral lobes are predominantly high-intensity white with localized low-intensity black mottling along the trailing edge and distal tips (corners).

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped notch with a calculated pixel-depth of approximately 15% of the total fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, low-amplitude serrations present across the entire trailing edge. The right lobe exhibits more pronounced jagged peaks (sawtooth pattern) compared to the left lobe which has a smoother, more worn topographic profile.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Symmetric convex curves at the leading edge tapering into a shallow concave sweep toward the median notch on the trailing edge.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Isolated dark pixel clusters (mottling) visible on the medial portion of the left lobe and distal edge of the right lobe, likely representing focal pigmentation or healed barnacle attachment sites.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Irregular jagged indentations on the trailing edge of the right lobe suggestive of minor physical trauma or environmental wear.
other_distinctive_markers: The right distal tip (corner) shows a concentrated region of low-intensity black pigment extending inward from the edge. A second whale's dorsal region is visible in the mid-ground right of the fluke.
